references.text: The command to tear down altars and cut down Asherah poles is given as part of God's instruction to Israel to remove idolatry from the land.
The command to tear down pagan altars and cut down Asherah poles is repeated as part of the legislation concerning pure worship.
God commands Israel to tear down the nations' altars and cut down their Asherah poles.
Continuation of the account where Gideon actually tears down the Baal altar and the Asherah pole, along with the consequences of this action.
Elijah challenges the people to choose between the Lord and Baal, presenting similar themes about removing Baal worship.
Jehu destroys the temple of Baal and the pillar of Baal, demonstrating fulfillment of God's will to remove idolatry.
King Josiah cleanses the temple and removes all objects associated with Baal and Asherah.
King Josiah begins to cleanse Judah of the high places, the Asherah poles, and the carved images.
